name: Dual On/Off Outlet
description: The on/off outlet with two separately controlled outlets, which runs the KeypadLinc code base with load sense for each outlet.

operatingFlags.name: programmingLock
operatingFlags.label: Programming lock
operatingFlags.description: Linking and programming from the device itself are locked out.

operatingFlags.name: ledOnTransmit
operatingFlags.label: Blink LED when sending
operatingFlags.description: The status LED blinks when the device sends an Insteon message.

operatingFlags.name: secondLoadSense
operatingFlags.label: Bottom outlet load sense
operatingFlags.description: Load sense is on for the bottom outlet, group 2.

operatingFlags.name: loadSense
operatingFlags.label: Top outlet load sense
operatingFlags.description: Load sense is on for the top outlet, group 1.

operatingFlags.name: ledOff
operatingFlags.label: LED off
operatingFlags.description: The status LEDs and button backlights are off.

verification.note: One source swaps 0x08 and 0x09 (backlight on and off); the values here are those other sources give. The Insteon Developer's Guide reads bit 4 of the 0x00 reply as LED on, but later sources read it as LED off, the state 0x08 sets.

operatingFlags.name: keyBeep
operatingFlags.label: Beep on button press
operatingFlags.description: The device beeps when a button is pressed.

operatingFlags.name: radioOff
operatingFlags.label: Turn off radio
operatingFlags.description: The device doesn't originate RF messages. It still repeats the RF messages it hears.

operatingFlags.name: powerLineOff
operatingFlags.label: Turn off powerline
operatingFlags.description: Insteon communication over the powerline is off. The device turns it back on whenever it powers up.

operatingFlags.name: x10Off
operatingFlags.label: Turn off X10
operatingFlags.description: X10 sending and receiving are off.

operatingFlags.name: errorBlink
operatingFlags.label: Blink LED on errors
operatingFlags.description: The status LED blinks when a communication error occurs.

operatingFlags.name: cleanupReport
operatingFlags.label: Send cleanup reports
operatingFlags.description: The device sends a success report after the cleanup messages that follow a group command.

operatingFlags.name: smartHops
operatingFlags.label: Smart hops
operatingFlags.description: Each message starts with the hop count of the last acknowledgment received (smart hops). When the bit is 0, each message starts with one hop.

readings.name: databaseDelta
readings.label: ALL-Link database changes
readings.description: A count that goes up whenever the ALL-Link database changes.

readings.name: crcErrorCount
readings.label: CRC errors
readings.description: The number of messages received with a CRC error.

verification.note: The Insteon Developer's Guide gives query 0x02 as a signal-to-noise value; later sources count messages with CRC errors there.

values.name: x10HouseCode
values.label: X10 house code
values.description: The X10 house code, or 0x20 for no X10 address.

values.name: ledBrightness
values.label: LED brightness
values.description: The brightness of the status LED, from 0x11 (dimmest) to 0x7F (brightest).

writes.name: x10Address
writes.description: Sets the X10 address of the top outlet (D1 0x01) or the bottom outlet (D1 0x02).

writes.name: ledBrightness
writes.description: Sets the brightness of the status LED.

parameter.name: state
parameter.description: 0x00 turns the top outlet off; 0x01 through 0xFF turn it on.

standardCommands.name: readStatus
standardCommands.description: Reads the top outlet's level. The acknowledgment's cmd1 carries the ALL-Link database delta.

standardCommands.name: readOutlets
standardCommands.description: Reads which outlets are on. The acknowledgment's cmd1 carries the ALL-Link database delta.

standardCommands.name: beep
standardCommands.description: Beeps once, as pressing the SET button does. The device ignores cmd2.

standardCommands.name: groupOn
standardCommands.description: Turns on an outlet as a group On would.

standardCommands.name: groupOff
standardCommands.description: Turns off an outlet as a group Off would.

extendedCommands.name: bottomOutletOn
extendedCommands.description: Turns the bottom outlet on. Any cmd2 from 0x01 through 0xFF turns it on, and 0x00 off.

responder.name: onLevel
responder.label: On or off
responder.description: 0x00 turns the load off when the controller's On arrives, 0xFF on.

verification.note: Data 1 and 2 are read from the On/Off Outlet Developer Notes; they don't say how a record picks the top or bottom outlet, so the records here are the same for both and the outlet a record switches may follow the controller's group. Inferred: seen on two i2CS devices (Outdoor On/Off Plug 2634-222 firmware 0x42, On/Off Plug 2635-222 firmware 0x48) linked to a Hub 2245, the device itself writes its responder record when it's linked remotely or with the SET button, and takes Data 1 from the load's state at that moment: the two plugs wrote 0x00 when the load was off and 0xFF when it was on. The On/Off Plug 2635-222 Owner's Manual says to make sure the module is on before linking it as a responder. The values given here are what to write when writing the record by hand.

responder.description: The ramp rate; the outlet switches at once.

notes: The On/Off Outlet Developer Notes mark bit 0 of the 0x05 reply reserved and lists no Set Operating Flags 0x10 or 0x11, so the application retries flag is left out; another source gives it for the KeypadLinc code base.
The On/Off Outlet Developer Notes give bit 4 of the 0x05 reply as the button lock; another source gives 0x18 to lock the buttons and 0x19 to unlock them.

valueTables.name: onOff
valueTables.description: Off and on, for a load or LED a record switches.
